sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova foundation models: Frontier intelligence and industry leading price performance
sources.evidence: December 3, 2024 launch announcement makes Nova Pro available through Bedrock, names amazon.nova-pro-v1:0, specifies 300K input tokens and tool/API workflows, and demonstrates PDF and video analysis. April 2025 update adds benchmark evaluations.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Section 1.1 explicitly describes Pro, Lite and Micro as Transformer-based. Pro accepts text, images, documents and video and generates text. Full PDF was retrieved and text-extracted after browser extraction exceeded its size limit; no total or active parameter counts or dense/MoE classification were found.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: April 30, 2025 addendum includes Nova Pro benchmark and runtime comparison columns, but no parameter-count or architectural specification for Pro. The current linked CDN copy was accessible; the old assets hostname returned 404.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: December 2, 2025 report contains exact Nova 1 Pro benchmark comparison rows. It supplies no total/active parameter counts or additional architectural detail for that model; Nova 2 specifications cannot be transferred to Nova 1 Pro.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: The later comparison's Table 1 gives Nova Pro's Params cell as NP, context 300k, and release month 12/24, rather than a numeric model size. Full PDF retrieved and extracted locally after the browser fetch timed out.

sources.title: Iterative Training — Understanding escrow buckets
sources.evidence: Explicitly states that Amazon Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow S3 buckets in AWS-managed accounts rather than being copied to customer accounts.

sources.title: Available foundation models — Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Table dated July 29, 2026 lists Nova Pro/nova-textgeneration-pro with AWS Service Terms and no inference instance types. Its broad Open-Weight Models tab also contains Nova rows, conflicting with Nova-specific proprietary/escrow documentation; tab placement is insufficient evidence of a public weights release.

sources.title: Complete request schema — Amazon Nova Version 1
sources.evidence: Current Version 1 request documentation explicitly labels reasoningConfig as available for Amazon Nova Pro and Amazon Nova Lite, with enable/disable and effort controls. It also describes toolConfig. The reasoning claim conflicts with the March 2026 migration table.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon Nova 1 to Amazon Nova 2 on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: March 18, 2026 migration table explicitly marks Extended Thinking No for Nova 1 Pro and Yes for Nova 2 Lite. Confirms 300K context, text/image/video inputs, and continued Converse-only document support.

sources.title: Understanding model reasoning with extended reasoning — Version 1
sources.evidence: Page expressly says Version 1 and explains extended reasoning, but both concrete examples use amazon.nova-lite-1-5-v1:0, not amazon.nova-pro-v1:0. This leaves the original Pro endpoint's support unresolved.

sources.title: Nova Pro — Amazon Bedrock model card
sources.evidence: Identifies Nova Pro as Amazon's model and maps it to amazon.nova-pro-v1:0. Confirms 300K context, text/image/video inputs and text output. Its launch date is December 5, 2024, later than the contemporaneous December 3 public launch.

sources.title: Additional resources — AWS Foundation Model Catalog
sources.evidence: The Nova Pro row maps to amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 with 300k context and text/image/video input. It lists December 2, 2024 as release date, conflicting with the contemporaneous December 3 announcement and the Bedrock card's December 5.

sources.title: Multimodal support for Amazon Nova — Version 1
sources.evidence: Version 1 documentation supports images, video and documents; PDF/DOCX media documents are accepted through Converse only and processed with interleaved text/image understanding.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier — AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Card scoped to the April 30, 2025 family confirms Nova membership, Transformer-based token inference, agentic/API use, and software-development use cases. It directs Nova users to AWS Service Terms. Premier is the most capable tier, making an unqualified current flagship claim for Pro misleading.

name.note: Exact developer model-card name; original endpoint amazon.nova-pro-v1:0.

developer.note: Developed by Amazon AGI; Amazon is the catalog-level developer.

family.note: Nova is the documented model family; Pro is its tier. Normalize the baseline tier-specific family slug.

release_date.note: Retain the contemporaneous public launch date. Later official catalog dates disagree: December 2 and December 5. Neither establishes earlier public availability than the explicit December 3 launch.

open_weights.note: Specific proprietary-weight and escrow statements outweigh broad JumpStart tab grouping. Customization access does not establish an open-weight release.

license.note: The exact Nova Pro JumpStart row names these terms; the Nova service card also directs users to them. This is proprietary service access, not an open-source weight license.

parameters_b.note: No numerical total count in the original, Premier or Nova 2 reports checked. The later MASSIVE-Agents exact Nova Pro comparison row gives Params as NP. Do not substitute third-party size estimates.

active_parameters_b.note: No active parameter count is separately reported for Nova Pro; no dense or MoE assumption is made.

architecture.note: Explicit Transformer architecture statement for Pro in section 1.1. Dense versus MoE and decoder/encoder details remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: Launch documentation and current exact-model card agree on 300K tokens.

modalities.note: Text/image/video are native input categories. Retain catalog PDF capability because the launch directly demonstrates it; PDF input requires Converse document handling.

reasoning.note: Unresolved primary-source conflict: current Version 1 schema explicitly enables reasoningConfig for Nova Pro, while March 18, 2026 migration table says Nova 1 Pro has no Extended Thinking. Version 1 examples use Lite 1.5, not original Pro. No exact-endpoint validation or release notice resolves this; clear false to null.

tool_call.note: Tool/function calling is explicitly documented. The migration table's lack of built-in tools concerns hosted web/code tools, not external function calling.

description.value: First-generation Amazon Nova multimodal model for document and video analysis, code generation, and tool-using applications.
description.note: Replace the unsupported current flagship positioning with documented capabilities and generation.

patch.description: First-generation Amazon Nova multimodal model for document and video analysis, code generation, and tool-using applications.

sources.label: Nova Pro terms in SageMaker catalog

patch.notes: Original endpoint: amazon.nova-pro-v1:0. Transformer-based; total/active counts and dense/MoE structure are undisclosed. Extended-thinking support is unresolved: current Version 1 schema names Pro as supporting reasoningConfig, but AWS's March 2026 migration table says Nova 1 Pro does not; the Version 1 examples use Lite 1.5. PDF input uses Converse. Public launch was December 3, 2024; later official listings show conflicting December 2/5 dates. Nova weights are proprietary despite broad JumpStart open-weight tab placement.

summary: Audited all 14 fields against exact-model and family-scoped primary evidence. Correct family, license and Transformer architecture; replace the flagship description. Preserve 300K context, modalities, tool calling, closed weights and December 3 public release. Original/Premier/Nova 2 reports and a later exact-model comparison provide no public total or active count. Explicitly clear reasoning to null because conflicting first-party statements cannot be resolved for the original Pro endpoint.
